descriptionChirho: The Aramaic cardinal number 'one' (חַד), used in Daniel and Ezra to count singular items — one horn (Dan 7:8; 8:3,9), one week (Dan 9:27), one beast (Dan 7:16), etc. Multilingual evidence is consistent: eng 'one', spa 'uno/una', hin 'एक', arb 'وَاحِد', kor '하나', swa 'moja'. Both masculine and feminine forms (חַד/חֲדָה) represent grammatical gender agreement, not distinct senses.

An idiomatic adverbial use of the Aramaic number 'one' with the preposition כְּ (כַּחֲדָה 'as one'), meaning 'together, all at once' (Ezra 4:3 or Dan 2:35). This is a lexicalized prepositional phrase distinct from the bare cardinal number. Multilingual evidence shows a shift from numeric to adverbial meaning: eng 'together', spa 'juntamente', hin 'एक–साथ', arb 'مَعًا', kor '함께', swa 'pamoja' — none of which render it as 'one'.
